The Navien NPE-240A2 is a condensing gas tankless water heater with a maximum input of 199,900 BTU/h and a 0.95 UEF. It delivers 8.7 GPM at a 45°F temperature rise and 5.6 GPM at a 67°F rise, and modulates down to 13,300 BTU/h. The A2 version has Navien's ComfortFlow recirculation pump and buffer tank built in; the NPE-240S2 has the same input without the pump and buffer tank. It mounts indoors or outdoors, runs on natural gas or propane, and vents in 2" or 3" pipe.

Key Features

  • Modulating input from 13,300 to 199,900 BTU/h on natural gas or propane
  • 0.95 UEF; ENERGY STAR certified
  • ComfortFlow built-in recirculation pump and buffer tank
  • Hot water flow: 11.2 GPM at a 35°F rise, 8.7 GPM at 45°F and 5.6 GPM at 67°F
  • Minimum activation flow 0.5 GPM; Navien also lists a < 0.01 GPM option
  • Primary and secondary stainless steel heat exchangers
  • Cabinet 17.3" W x 27.4" H x 13.2" D, 77 lbs

Applications

  • Whole-house domestic hot water; size on the 67°F figure where incoming water is cold
  • Homes that want hot water recirculation without adding an external pump
  • Replacing a storage tank water heater where a gas line, vent route and condensate drain are available
  • Residential and commercial hot water loads within the rated flow

Before You Order

  • Gas type: listed for natural gas and propane (NG/LP convertible). Confirm which gas the unit is set up for, and have any conversion done by a licensed installer following the Navien manual.
  • Gas line: 3/4" gas connection. The meter and line must supply the full 199,900 BTU/h; supply pressure is 3.5" to 10.5" WC on natural gas and 8" to 13" WC on propane.
  • Venting: 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC, approved polypropylene or stainless steel for intake and exhaust, 0" clearance to combustibles.
  • Electrical: 120V AC, 60 Hz supply at the unit.
  • Water: 3/4" cold inlet and 3/4" hot outlet; water pressure 15 to 150 PSI.
  • Condensate: this is a condensing appliance and produces acidic condensate. Plan a drain line to a suitable drain, with a neutralizer where local code requires one.
  • Altitude: approved to 10,100 ft on natural gas or propane; see the installation manual for high-altitude settings.

How much hot water you actually get

Navien rates every tankless unit by temperature rise, because the colder the incoming water, the less of it one burner can heat. Here is what the NPE-240A2 delivers:

Temperature rise Flow rate Typical use
35°F 11.2 GPM Warm-climate groundwater, or a preheated feed
45°F 8.7 GPM The usual design point across most of the U.S.
67°F 5.6 GPM Northern winter, incoming water near 40°F

Sized against a 2.5 GPM showerhead, the 67°F column is worth roughly 2 showers at once on the coldest day of the year, and more than that the rest of the year. Size to the 67°F row if your winter groundwater runs cold.

Minimum activation flow is 0.5 GPM, so it fires for a hand wash, not just a full shower.

With a Navien recirculation setup this unit also supports the low-flow activation option, down to under 0.01 GPM.

About ComfortFlow®: the pump and the buffer tank are inside the unit, not bolted on. That is what kills the cold-water sandwich when someone turns the shower off and back on, and it lets you run recirculation on a dedicated return line or on a crossover valve at the far fixture.

Frequently asked questions

How many showers can the Navien NPE-240S2 run at once?

Navien rates the NPE-240S2 at 5.8 GPM at a 67°F temperature rise and 8.7 GPM at a 45°F rise. With 2.5 GPM showerheads that is roughly two showers at once on the coldest day of the year, and more the rest of the year.

Does the NPE-240S2 run on propane?

Yes. The unit is certified for both natural gas and propane, with a modulating input of 13,300 to 199,900 BTU/h.

What venting does the NPE-240S2 need?

Intake and exhaust run in 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless steel, with 0" clearance to combustibles. Gas, venting and condensate work must be done by a licensed installer to the Navien manual and local code.

What is the difference between the NPE-240S2 and the NPE-240A2?

They share the same cabinet and dual stainless steel heat exchangers. The NPE-240A2 adds an internal recirculation pump; the NPE-240S2 has no pump and carries the higher efficiency rating, 0.96 UEF.

The IBC SFC 199 is a wall-hung condensing combi boiler that supplies space heating and domestic hot water from one unit, on natural gas or propane. Domestic hot water input is up to 199,000 BTU/h and space heating input is up to 125,000 BTU/h, with 95% AFUE. It delivers 5.0 GPM of hot water at a 67°F temperature rise. Venting is 2" up to 65 ft or 3" up to 120 ft equivalent length. No circulator is included.

Key Features

  • Domestic hot water input up to 199,000 BTU/h; space heating input up to 125,000 BTU/h
  • 95% AFUE; ASME-rated heat exchanger with 2 independent copper waterways in a cast aluminum block
  • Hot water delivery 5.0 GPM at a 67°F rise, up to 7 GPM maximum; activates at 0.5 GPM
  • No 3-way valve or secondary DHW plate heat exchanger; built-in bypass valve
  • Touchscreen control with outdoor reset; accepts a 0-10 VDC signal; wireless cascade up to 8 units
  • Factory-installed domestic water strainer; compatible with standard propylene glycol
  • Approved for installation up to 10,000 ft

Applications

  • Homes where one appliance provides space heating and domestic hot water
  • Replacing a boiler and a separate water heater
  • Cascaded installations of up to 8 units
  • Installations at elevations up to 10,000 ft

Before You Order

  • Gas type: natural gas or propane. Confirm which gas the unit is set up for and how conversion is done in the IBC manual.
  • Gas line: 3/4" gas inlet; supply pressure 4" to 14" WC. Size the line for the full 199,000 BTU/h.
  • Venting: 2" up to 65 ft or 3" up to 120 ft equivalent length on each side, in PVC or polypropylene; a 2" vent adapter is used for 2" venting per IBC.
  • Electrical: 120V, 60 Hz; 120 W at full fire.
  • Water: 3/4" heating connections. Maximum operating pressure 43.5 psig heating and 150 psig domestic. Confirm the domestic connection size in the IBC manual.
  • Pump: no circulator is included.
  • Condensate: this is a condensing appliance and produces acidic condensate. Plan a drain line to a suitable drain, with a neutralizer where local code requires one.

The AquaFlow AF-40 is a 40-gallon indirect-fired water heater. It has no burner: domestic water is heated by boiler water passing through an internal coil. The tank is AISI 444 stainless steel with a 316L stainless steel coil and 2" of rigid polyurethane foam insulation. This model is listed with a 120,000 BTU maximum input. Cold and hot connections are 3/4" and tank connections are 1".

Key Features

  • AISI 444 stainless steel tank
  • 316L stainless steel heat exchanger coil
  • Butt-welded construction, pickled and passivated inside and out
  • No sacrificial anode required
  • Dedicated recirculation connection
  • 2" rigid polyurethane foam insulation
  • Listed maximum input 120,000 BTU

Applications

  • Domestic hot water from a hydronic boiler, piped as its own zone
  • Solar and heat-recovery systems
  • Replacing an existing indirect tank of similar size

Before You Order

  • Heat source: the boiler or other heat source must be able to supply the required input, with a zone or circulator for the tank.
  • Connections: 3/4" cold and hot, 1" tank connections; check locations on the drawings.
  • Space: take height and diameter from the drawings and submittal linked under Documents.
  • Controls and safety: confirm how the tank thermostat or sensor ties into the boiler control, and whether a T&P relief valve is supplied.
  • No gas line or vent is needed at the tank itself.

The Navien NPE-180S2 is a condensing gas tankless water heater with a maximum input of 150,000 BTU/h and a 0.96 UEF. It delivers 6.5 GPM at a 45°F temperature rise and 4.3 GPM at a 67°F rise, and modulates down to 10,000 BTU/h. The S2 version has no built-in recirculation pump or buffer tank; the NPE-180A2 is the same input size with both built in. It mounts indoors or outdoors, runs on natural gas or propane, and vents in 2" or 3" pipe.

Key Features

  • Modulating input from 10,000 to 150,000 BTU/h on natural gas or propane
  • 0.96 UEF; ENERGY STAR certified
  • No internal recirculation pump or buffer tank
  • Hot water flow: 8.4 GPM at a 35°F rise, 6.5 GPM at 45°F and 4.3 GPM at 67°F
  • Minimum activation flow 0.5 GPM
  • Primary and secondary stainless steel heat exchangers
  • Cabinet 17.3" W x 27.4" H x 13.2" D, 68 lbs

Applications

  • Whole-house domestic hot water; size on the 67°F figure where incoming water is cold
  • Installations that do not need built-in recirculation
  • Replacing a storage tank water heater where a gas line, vent route and condensate drain are available
  • Residential and commercial hot water loads within the rated flow

Before You Order

  • Gas type: listed for natural gas and propane (NG/LP convertible). Confirm which gas the unit is set up for, and have any conversion done by a licensed installer following the Navien manual.
  • Gas line: 3/4" gas connection. The meter and line must supply the full 150,000 BTU/h; supply pressure is 3.5" to 10.5" WC on natural gas and 8" to 13" WC on propane.
  • Venting: 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC, approved polypropylene or stainless steel for intake and exhaust, 0" clearance to combustibles.
  • Electrical: 120V AC, 60 Hz supply at the unit.
  • Water: 3/4" cold inlet and 3/4" hot outlet; water pressure 15 to 150 PSI.
  • Condensate: this is a condensing appliance and produces acidic condensate. Plan a drain line to a suitable drain, with a neutralizer where local code requires one.
  • Altitude: approved to 10,100 ft on natural gas or propane; see the installation manual for high-altitude settings.

How much hot water you actually get

Navien rates every tankless unit by temperature rise, because the colder the incoming water, the less of it one burner can heat. Here is what the NPE-180S2 delivers:

Temperature rise Flow rate Typical use
35°F 8.4 GPM Warm-climate groundwater, or a preheated feed
45°F 6.5 GPM The usual design point across most of the U.S.
67°F 4.3 GPM Northern winter, incoming water near 40°F

Sized against a 2.5 GPM showerhead, the 67°F column is worth roughly one shower on the coldest day of the year, and more than that the rest of the year. Size to the 67°F row if your winter groundwater runs cold.

Minimum activation flow is 0.5 GPM, so it fires for a hand wash, not just a full shower.

The Heat-Flo HF-40 is a 40-gallon indirect water heater with all connections on top. It has no burner or element: boiler water passes through an internal coil and heats the domestic water stored in the tank. It is installed as a zone on a hydronic boiler, with its own circulator or zone valve.

Key Features

  • 40-gallon storage
  • All connections on top of the tank
  • Internal coil heated by boiler water
  • No burner, element or vent at the tank

Applications

  • Domestic hot water from a hydronic boiler, piped as its own zone
  • Replacing an existing 40-gallon indirect tank
  • Installations where top connections suit the piping layout

Before You Order

  • Heat source: the boiler needs enough output and a dedicated zone or circulator for the tank.
  • Connections: all on top. Confirm the sizes on the Heat-Flo specification sheet linked under Documents.
  • Space: take height and diameter from the Heat-Flo specification sheet linked under Documents.
  • Controls and safety: confirm whether an aquastat or sensor well and a T&P relief valve are supplied.
  • No gas line, vent or electrical supply is needed at the tank itself.
